floor_history.headline: Recon s1: canonical island respell (func_800274BC form) lowered floor 33->30 with insn parity 144==144; full residual map banked; disc-copy survival is the frontier head.

s1 frontier head CLOSED: combine (not cse) folds the disc copy; an if/else-spelled LZCS guard makes it survive at zero insn cost, landing in $a0 (target's register) in the beqz delay slot. Floor still

Floor 30 -> 7 at unchanged parity 144==144: reusing sqrt_val in place for the <<9 and naming the first quotient's numerator fixed the entire downstream allocation cascade; residual is 6 slots of disc-

Permuter modality exhausted on the v21 chassis: 33,881 random iterations (zero finds, base never beaten) plus an exhaustive 24-point directed PERM cross-product (none below base) prove floor 7 is a st

frontier.hypothesis: Getting `disc` (pseudo 117) allocated to $a2/$6 instead of $v1/$3 closes 6 of the remaining 7 slots and is still the head of everything left - but it is now proven NOT reachable by respelling the guard region, so the attack must be on the allocno ORDER itself.
frontier.mechanism: global.c sorts allocnos by roughly log2(n_refs)*n_refs/live_length. 117 has 5 refs across a 6-insn live range, which makes it the FIRST of 24 allocated, and `;; 117 preferences: 3` then hands it $3 before any other allocno is considered. Target's disc is live ~6 slots longer (its bltz reads disc where ours reads the copy), which both lowers its priority and removes the early pick of $3. s4 proved the live-range lengthening cannot be bought by any spelling of the guard/exit/index axes at zero instruction cost.
frontier.next_probe: FORENSICS, not search. Run `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8002D518` on the v21 chassis and read .greg: (i) print the full sorted allocno list with each one's n_refs and live_length, and compute by hand which single perturbation of 117's live_length or n_refs would sort it below the allocno that currently takes $6; (ii) then work BACKWARDS from that number to what source-visible property would produce it, instead of forwards from spellings. (iii) Separately read set_preference's input: identify WHICH mflo pseudo local-alloc put in $3 (the dispositions line) and whether re-associating the discriminant so that operand lands elsewhere removes 117's $3 preference outright - that is a different lever from live-range length and has never been measured.

frontier.hypothesis: Slot 88 needs `if (disc < 0) return 0;` and the only thing stopping it is jump2 cross-jumping the resulting 2-insn block into the entrance return-0 block (142 insns vs target's 144).
frontier.mechanism: GCC emits `(set (reg 2) 0); (jump epilogue)` for a `return 0;` statement, which is exactly target slots 87/88. jump.c's cross-jump finds the identical tail in the entrance chain and redirects the conditional branch there, deleting the block. Both target AND our build already carry TWO un-merged copies of that same block in the entrance chain, so cross-jump here is SELECTIVE rather than exhaustive - something about the third instance makes it mergeable. s4 added the `goto`-a-shared-end spelling to the measured set and it is no better than `result = 0;`.
frontier.next_probe: Recompile the v21 chassis with `pwsh tools/grinder/dump.ps1 func_8002D518` and read .jump2 to see WHICH pair find_cross_jump matched and why the two existing entrance copies are not merged with each other. The productive question is what property distinguishes the surviving pair - once that is known, spell the disc<0 arm so it acquires the same property. Do NOT spend further probes on respelling `return 0` itself; the emitted shape is already correct and the exit-shape axis is now exhausted (s4 H13).

frontier.hypothesis: There is no third residual item - once the two above land the function is at 0.
frontier.mechanism: The v21 alignment is a complete 154-slot comparison with only 15 raw differing words, 8 of them scorer-masked classes (4 j-targets, 4 %hi/%lo D_8008D118 reloc words). Every remaining word is accounted for by the two items above. No ordering difference, no instruction-count difference, no missing or extra instruction anywhere - and the s4 workspace validation independently reproduced exactly that diff from a completely separate build path.
frontier.next_probe: After any change, re-run `tmp/grind/func_8002D518/s3/align.py <variant>` on an `objdump -dz` listing and confirm the raw-diff count equals engine score + 8; if it does not, a new masked class has appeared and must be identified before drawing conclusions.
